newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania's BCR bank raises again deposit rates.
newsitem.headline: Romania's BCR bank raises again deposit rates.

text.p: Romanian state-owned bank Banca Comerciala Romana SA (BCR) will again raise interest rates, in a bid to protect depositors against surging inflation and following upswings in the central bank's key rates.
The bank's rates on individuals' one-month deposits will rise to an annual 60 percent starting next Monday, up from a previous 53 percent, a BCR statement said on Thursday.
BCR's six-month and one-year rates will go up by 7.0 points to 62 and 63 percent, respectively. It will pay 61 percent on three-month deposits, up from 55 percent.

Year-on-year inflation, which quickened to 56.9 percent last year from 27.8 percent in 1995, is forecast to jump to 97 percent this year, led by January's fuel price rise and planned liberalisation of electicity and food prices.
The BCR raised deposit rates last month in line with a central bank drive to tighten monetary policies amid rising inflationary expectations.
The central bank's one-week refinancing rate rose to 90 percent last week from a previous 81 percent and compared with 53 percent earlier this year.
